# 7. Typed classes generated by a command, on top of the codec

Date: 2026-11-21

## Status

Accepted. Fills in the code generation that ADR 2 planned as a later minor version.

## Context

The values of ADR 2 are generic: a record is a `Map<String, Object?>`. The first consumer, `axt_protocol` in `paxel/axt-dart`, embeds the JSON texts of about 20 AXT record types (`lib/src/schemas.g.dart`, written by its own command-line tool) and has no typed classes for them. Every union in the AXT types is `["null", X]`. Their enum symbols are upper snake case (`DEVICE_ADD`), their field names snake case (`offset_seconds`), and three of their type names clash with `dart:core` (`axt.DateTime`, `axt.Duration`, `axt.Error`). Each AXT file defines the types it uses inline, so one type is defined in several files.

## Decision

- **Command.** `dart run avro:generate <schemas…> -o <file>`, a command of this package, writes one committed Dart library per run. It adds no dependency to `avro`; there is no `build_runner` builder.
- **Records.** A record becomes an immutable `final class`:
  - `final` fields and a `const` constructor with named parameters
  - non-nullable fields `required`; nullable fields optional, defaulting to `null`; Avro defaults stay for resolution only, as with `encode`
  - `==`, `hashCode`, `toString` and `copyWith`
- **Codec.** `avro` gains a generic `TypedCodec<T>`. Each generated class has a descriptor, `Xxx.avroType`, holding the schema, `toAvro` and `fromAvro`:
  - `TypedCodec(Xxx.avroType, writer: …)` resolves like `AvroCodec`
  - it offers `encode`, `decode` and the single-object methods
  - `codec.avro` is the underlying `AvroCodec`, for container files
- **Unions.** `["null", X]` becomes `X?`. Any other union becomes `Object?`, holding the generic value or a `Branch`.
- **Enums.** An Avro enum becomes a Dart `enum` with lowerCamelCase values, each carrying its symbol as `.symbol`.
- **Names.**
  - A class takes the simple name of its schema. `--prefix <namespace>=<Prefix>` prefixes the types of a namespace, so `--prefix axt=Axt` gives `AxtDateTime`.
  - Fields become lowerCamelCase. A Dart reserved word or a generated member gets a `$` suffix.
  - Two names that convert to the same name, or a clash with `dart:core`, stop the generator.
- **Schema text.** The generated code carries the verbatim JSON text of each `.avsc` file, `doc` and attributes included, parsed once on first use. A named type defined inline carries its own JSON part.
- **Duplicates.** A full name defined in several files gets one class when the canonical forms match. The first definition in file order wins, and the generator warns when `doc` or attributes differ; different fields stop it.
- **Other types.** Arrays and maps become `List<T>` and `Map<String, T>`; `bytes` and `fixed` become `Uint8List`; logical types follow ADR 3; inline named types get classes of their own.

## Considered options

- A `build_runner` builder in a separate `avro_generator` package: it would bring `build`, `source_gen` and `analyzer`, and a second package to publish. It can still be built on the same code later.
- Mutable classes, or Dart record typedefs: no value equality, or no documentation and no names.
- A sealed class per union: none of the AXT unions needs one. Moving from `Object?` to sealed classes later is a breaking change of the generated code.
- Enum values as the symbols, or field names unchanged: both need an `ignore` for the strict lints.
- Avro defaults as constructor defaults: defaults belong to resolution, as ADR 2 says for `encode`.

## Consequences

- Generated files are reviewed and committed like any other source. A change of the schemas means running the command again.
- Code generated by 0.2.0 depends on `TypedCodec` and the descriptor type of `avro` 0.2.0 or later.
